items.title: Recommendation letters on demand
items.ko: 독립 연구자 모임이 추천서를 얻기 위해 공동 연구를 제공하는 것이 비윤리적인지 묻고 답이 달렸어요.

paragraphs.en: The asker describes a small group of hard-working independent researchers and academics with scholarly publication experience, most of whom teach and do consulting work. Because they work mostly without supervisors, many of them find it hard to obtain recommendation letters for academic posts or fellowships. They are also reluctant to ask colleagues and students. So the group offers anyone who is possibly qualified the chance to work on collaborative projects aimed solely at producing a good recommendation letter for participants. The asker stresses that it is not commercial, that participants work as academic researchers, and asks whether anyone would consider the scheme unethical.
paragraphs.ko: 질문자는 학술 논문 발표 경험이 있고 대부분 가르치거나 컨설팅을 하는, 열심히 일하는 독립 연구자·학자의 작은 모임을 소개해요. 대개 지도자 없이 일하다 보니, 학계 자리나 펠로십에 필요한 추천서를 구하기 어렵다는 거예요. 동료나 학생에게 부탁하는 것도 꺼려진다고 해요. 그래서 이 모임은 자격이 있을 만한 누구에게든, 참가자에게 좋은 추천서를 써 주는 것만을 목표로 한 공동 프로젝트에 참여할 기회를 제안해요. 질문자는 상업적 활동이 아니며 참가자들이 학술 연구자로서 일한다고 강조하고, 이 계획이 비윤리적이라고 볼 사람이 있는지 물어요.

sents.en: The asker describes a small group of hard-working independent researchers and academics with scholarly publication experience, most of whom teach and do consulting work.
sents.ko: 질문자는 학술 논문 발표 경험이 있고 대부분 가르치거나 컨설팅을 하는, 열심히 일하는 독립 연구자·학자의 작은 모임을 소개해요.

sents.en: The asker stresses that it is not commercial, that participants work as academic researchers, and asks whether anyone would consider the scheme unethical.
sents.ko: 질문자는 상업적 활동이 아니며 참가자들이 학술 연구자로서 일한다고 강조하고, 이 계획이 비윤리적이라고 볼 사람이 있는지 물어요.

paragraphs.en: The one answer says there is nothing unethical about building a network of collaborators who can later write letters for you, and encourages independent researchers to do exactly that. But the answerer is concerned by the asker's comment describing the letter as a "reward" for doing unpaid academic work. What if someone does the work poorly, and is the group still obliged to write a letter, or a strong one? What if two participants write letters for each other, and can one write a negative letter without worrying about what the other will write?
paragraphs.ko: 유일한 답은 나중에 추천서를 써 줄 협력자 네트워크를 쌓는 데는 비윤리적인 것이 전혀 없다며, 독립 연구자들이 바로 그렇게 하길 권해요. 하지만 답변자는 추천서를 무급 학술 작업의 '보상'이라고 한 질문자의 댓글이 마음에 걸린다고 해요. 누군가 일을 형편없이 했다면 그래도 추천서, 그것도 강한 추천서를 써야 하느냐고 묻고 있어요. 두 참가자가 서로 추천서를 써 주는 경우, 상대가 무엇을 쓸지 걱정하지 않고 부정적인 추천서를 쓸 수 있느냐고도 물어요.

sents.en: The one answer says there is nothing unethical about building a network of collaborators who can later write letters for you, and encourages independent researchers to do exactly that.
sents.ko: 유일한 답은 나중에 추천서를 써 줄 협력자 네트워크를 쌓는 데는 비윤리적인 것이 전혀 없다며, 독립 연구자들이 바로 그렇게 하길 권해요.

sents.ko: 하지만 답변자는 추천서를 무급 학술 작업의 '보상'이라고 한 질문자의 댓글이 마음에 걸린다고 해요.

paragraphs.en: The answer says that creating opportunities for academics to work together is good, but promising a good letter as the compensation for work raises ethical concerns. The answerer would be much more comfortable with an arrangement that promised an honest assessment of someone's work. As an example, students who do research with the answerer can expect a letter, but the research takes center stage and the point of working together is not the letter. A useful lesson is the difference between a letter that is an honest by-product of real work and one that is promised as payment.

items.title: I've seen vs I saw this video before
items.ko: '이 영상 전에 본 적 있어요'를 현재완료 대신 과거형 saw로 말해도 되는지, 미국 영어 차이인지 묻는 글이에요.

paragraphs.en: The asker begins with a sentence of their own, "I saw this video before," said about a video clip they had come across, and wonders why the simple past appears there rather than the present perfect. They quote a rule from Swan's Practical English Usage: for finished events with words that mean "at some time up to now," such as ever, before, never, yet, recently, lately and already, the present perfect is normal in British English, as in "I'm sure we've met before." The question is whether the simple past "saw" in the sentence is an Americanism, used where British speakers would say "have already seen."

items.title: He still speaks like the man who he was when I met him
items.ko: 'the man who/that he was'에서 관계대명사 who를 써도 되는지 묻고, 답은 who와 which를 나눠 쓰라고 해요.

paragraphs.en: The asker examines a sentence about a man who still speaks the way he did when they first met: "He still speaks like the man (that / ?who) he was when I met him." The antecedent, "the man," is a person, and the relative pronoun functions as a nominal predicate inside the subordinate clause, so the asker asks whether who is allowed. For comparison, the asker offers a second sentence, "She looked like a grocer, which / ✱who she was," in which who seems wrong.
paragraphs.ko: 질문자는 처음 만났을 때처럼 아직도 말하는 한 남자에 관한 문장 'He still speaks like the man (that / ?who) he was when I met him'을 따져 봐요. 선행사 'the man'은 사람이고, 관계대명사는 종속절 안에서 명사 서술어 역할을 하니, who를 써도 되는지 묻는 거예요. 비교를 위해 두 번째 문장 'She looked like a grocer, which / ✱who she was'를 드는데, 여기서는 who가 틀려 보여요.

sents.en: The asker examines a sentence about a man who still speaks the way he did when they first met: "He still speaks like the man (that / ?who) he was when I met him."

paragraphs.en: The one answer says to use who in the first sentence and which in the second. The lesson for learners is that who suits a personal antecedent, while which fits a clause that comments on a whole statement.

items.title: Ignoring all the logistical advantages of the musket in combat would a musketeer outperform a trained archer in colonial america?
items.ko: 식민지 시대 미국에서 보급 이점을 빼면 머스킷 병사가 숙련된 궁수보다 강했을지 묻는 글이에요. 아직 답이 없어요.

paragraphs.en: The asker says their school taught the colonization of America with a number of inaccuracies that they are now trying to correct for themselves. One of them, they feel, was the weight given to the gun in Europe's ability to colonize, when disease had ravaged Native Americans so thoroughly before most colonization happened. They suspect the school also stressed the wrong advantages, because the musket's main edge seems to have been logistical: how quickly a recruit could be trained and how much easier bullets were to supply than arrows.
paragraphs.ko: 질문자는 학교가 미국 식민화를 가르칠 때 부정확한 부분이 여럿 있어서 지금 스스로 바로잡으려는 중이라고 말해요. 그중 하나는 대부분의 식민화가 이뤄지기 전에 질병이 원주민들을 철저히 휩쓸었는데도 유럽의 식민 능력에서 총의 비중을 지나치게 강조했다는 점이라고 느껴요. 질문자는 머스킷의 주된 강점이 병참에 있었던 듯하다며, 즉 신병을 얼마나 빨리 훈련시킬 수 있고 총알이 화살보다 얼마나 공급하기 쉬운지였다며, 학교가 엉뚱한 이점을 강조했다고 의심해요.

sents.en: They suspect the school also stressed the wrong advantages, because the musket's main edge seems to have been logistical: how quickly a recruit could be trained and how much easier bullets were to supply than arrows.

paragraphs.en: By contrast, the school presented muskets as vastly superior in combat and ignored such considerations entirely. The one real advantage it did mention was that muskets are not stopped by armor, but the asker notes that no musketeer wore armor on arriving in America, so any Native American archer would not have faced that problem.
paragraphs.ko: 반면 학교는 머스킷이 전투에서 압도적으로 우월했다고 가르치고 그런 고려는 전혀 다루지 않았어요. 학교가 언급한 유일한 실질적 이점은 머스킷이 갑옷에 막히지 않는다는 것이었지만, 질문자는 미국에 온 머스킷 병사 누구도 갑옷을 입지 않았으니 원주민 궁수는 그 문제를 겪지 않았을 것이라고 지적해요.

paragraphs.en: The question is therefore a thought experiment: take the same number of fully trained archers and musketeers, each with enough ammunition, and ask whether the musketeers would handily fell the archers or whether it would be a closer contest. items.title: What is the difference between nominal and real interest rates for a saver?
items.ko: 은행 금리 8%에 물가 상승 5%일 때 명목금리와 실질금리 차이를 어떻게 보는지 묻는 글이에요.

paragraphs.en: The asker's bank advertises a savings rate of 8 percent a year, while inflation is running at about 5 percent a year. They have read that the difference between nominal and real interest rates matters here but are unsure how to apply it. They ask whether the real rate simply means subtracting inflation from the advertised rate, so that their savings grow by only about 3 percent in real terms. They also ask whether, when inflation is high, they should compare savings accounts by real rate rather than by the advertised rate.
paragraphs.ko: 질문자의 은행은 연 8퍼센트의 저축 금리를 내세우는데 물가 상승률은 연 5퍼센트쯤 돼요. 질문자는 명목금리와 실질금리의 차이가 여기서 중요하다고 읽었지만 어떻게 적용할지 몰라요. 실질금리가 광고된 금리에서 물가 상승률을 빼는 것이라 저축이 실질적으로 3퍼센트쯤만 불어난다는 뜻인지 물어요. 또 물가 상승이 높을 때 저축 계좌를 광고된 금리가 아니라 실질금리로 비교해야 하는지도 물어요.

sents.en: The asker's bank advertises a savings rate of 8 percent a year, while inflation is running at about 5 percent a year.
sents.ko: 질문자의 은행은 연 8퍼센트의 저축 금리를 내세우는데 물가 상승률은 연 5퍼센트쯤 돼요.

sents.en: They have read that the difference between nominal and real interest rates matters here but are unsure how to apply it.

sents.en: They ask whether the real rate simply means subtracting inflation from the advertised rate, so that their savings grow by only about 3 percent in real terms.
sents.ko: 실질금리가 광고된 금리에서 물가 상승률을 빼는 것이라 저축이 실질적으로 3퍼센트쯤만 불어난다는 뜻인지 물어요.

sents.en: They also ask whether, when inflation is high, they should compare savings accounts by real rate rather than by the advertised rate.
sents.ko: 또 물가 상승이 높을 때 저축 계좌를 광고된 금리가 아니라 실질금리로 비교해야 하는지도 물어요.

paragraphs.en: The one answer says there is no reason to compare real rates between offers. When two offers are compared, the inflation term is the same in both calculations, so you can safely compare nominal rates only and pick the best one. The answerer adds that inflation and the real rate matter more for how they affect your savings and debt. If inflation turns out higher than expected, money in an 8 percent savings account earns lower real returns, while a fixed-rate loan becomes cheaper in real terms.
paragraphs.ko: 유일한 답은 상품들 사이에서 실질금리를 비교할 이유가 없다고 말해요. 두 상품을 비교할 때 물가 상승 항목은 두 계산에 똑같이 들어가므로 명목금리만 비교해 가장 좋은 것을 골라도 안전해요. 답변자는 물가 상승과 실질금리가 오히려 저축과 빚에 어떤 영향을 주는지 볼 때 더 중요하다고 덧붙여요. 물가 상승이 예상보다 높게 나오면 8퍼센트 저축 계좌의 돈은 실질 수익이 낮아지는 반면 고정금리 대출은 실질적으로 더 싸져요.

items.title: What should I consider when choosing the right cooking oil for everyday meals?

paragraphs.en: The asker says they regularly prepare meals at home and want to understand how to choose the right cooking oil for everyday use. They ask whether there are particular factors worth weighing, and they name three: the smoke point, the flavour of the oil, and the type of cooking method. The asker is also interested in the differences between commonly available cooking oils and in when each one is most suitable.
paragraphs.ko: 질문자는 집에서 자주 식사를 준비하는데, 매일 쓰기에 알맞은 요리용 기름을 고르는 법을 알고 싶다고 해요. 그는 따져 볼 만한 요소가 따로 있는지 묻고 세 가지를 꼽는데, 연기가 나기 시작하는 온도(발연점), 기름의 맛과 향, 조리 방법의 종류예요. 질문자는 또 흔히 구할 수 있는 요리용 기름들의 차이와, 각각 언제 가장 알맞은지에도 관심이 있어요.

sents.en: The asker says they regularly prepare meals at home and want to understand how to choose the right cooking oil for everyday use.
sents.ko: 질문자는 집에서 자주 식사를 준비하는데, 매일 쓰기에 알맞은 요리용 기름을 고르는 법을 알고 싶다고 해요.

items.title: What's the most common pronunciation of "what's the"?

paragraphs.en: The asker wonders whether the formal sound of the "'s th" part in "what's the" is actually pronounced when a speaker does not want to be overly correct. The asker says that what they seem to hear is something like /wɒtzə/, with the "s" and "th" blending into a single "z" sound, but admits to being nowhere near sure. The question also asks that any answer based on a specific dialect, such as British, American or Australian English, say which one it refers to. At the time of reading, the question had no answers yet, and it had been voted down to a score of minus three. For learners, the useful lesson is that the spoken form of a phrase can differ from its written form, and that listeners often rely on context rather than on every individual sound.

items.title: Rule of thumb for spending on grocerries
items.ko: 새 나라로 이사해 장을 보고 놀란 사람이 소득 대비 식료품비와 비상금의 기준을 물어요.

paragraphs.en: The asker recently moved to a new country and went grocery shopping, and was shocked to find the bill came to one and a half fifths of their pay. That bill did not even cover the whole shop, since fresh meat had not been counted. The asker says this made them feel shaky and sad, because it suggests they have no logic or rule for deciding how much to spend on groceries and how much to save for emergencies. To top it off, the asker's children keep asking for things, and saying no makes the asker feel bad. items.title: Why do stars twinkle but planets usually do not?
items.ko: 별은 반짝이는데 행성은 왜 대체로 안 그런지 묻는 글이에요(아직 답 없음).

paragraphs.en: A reader of Astronomy Stack Exchange asks why stars twinkle but planets usually do not, and at the time of writing the question has no answers yet. The asker points out that on a clear night, stars seem to twinkle and change brightness from moment to moment, while planets usually shine with a steadier light. The asker wonders whether the difference is mainly because stars are point sources of light while planets appear as tiny discs, or whether the Earth's atmosphere affects them in different ways. The goal, in the asker's words, is to understand the physics behind the twinkling and why planets are less affected. Because no answer has been posted, there is no explanation to report yet, but the question itself gives learners useful phrases such as point source, tiny disc and steadier light.
